## How to Use the Presentations

- Press `space` or the down arrow ($\downarrow$) to go to the next slide or reveal hidden content.
- Press the up arrow ($\uparrow$) or `P` to go to the previous slide.
- Press the right or left arrow to move to the next or previous chapter.
- See more shortcuts [here](https://defkey.com/reveal-js-shortcuts).
- On mobile devices, you can swipe to change slides.

These slide decks are built with [11 tools and languages](#how-the-lectures-were-made), including `R`, `Python`, `Bash`, `LaTeX`, `JavaScript`, and `Markdown`. The `qdraw` plugin by [Abdullah Al Mahmud](https://www.thinkermahmud.com/qdraw/) is also available on every slide, for live annotation.

## How the Lectures Were Made

<center>
<i style="font-size:10.5em; float: right; padding: 10px;" class="fa-solid fa-dice"></i>
</center>

All the lecture slides were first built with the `rmarkdown` and [`revealjs`](https://revealjs.com/) packages for the [R programming language](https://www.r-project.org/), inside the [RStudio IDE](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). `rmarkdown` rendered `.Rmd` files into HTML. The slides are now rendered with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/) instead, from `.qmd` files.

![From plain-text source to a live slide deck: Quarto renders Markdown, R and LaTeX into HTML, CSS and JavaScript, all tracked with Git.](img/lecture-toolchain.svg){fig-alt="Diagram: Markdown, R code chunks, LaTeX math and YAML front matter are rendered by Quarto with reveal.js into HTML slides, CSS styling, JavaScript interactivity and qdraw annotation, all tracked with Git and Bash/fish."}

The following languages, markup formats, and tools go into building each presentation:

* **HTML** (HyperText Markup Language): the standard markup language for web pages. The output files are HTML, generated mainly from `.qmd` sources, though raw HTML is occasionally used directly.
* **CSS** (Cascading Style Sheets): the stylesheet language behind the site's design, heavily customized to match Stat Mania's look.
* **JavaScript**: powers the slides' interactivity, both for dynamic content loading and as part of the HTML output that `revealjs` generates.
* **R**: used for data generation and computation inside the slides.
* **Python**: used in scripts that generate some of the source files (e.g. quiz banks and puzzle data).
* **LaTeX**: used for typesetting mathematical expressions.
* **Markdown**: the lightweight markup language the source files are written in.
* **Git**: the distributed version control system used to track every change to the source.
* **Bash / fish shell**: the command-line tools used for file operations and for running Quarto and Git.
* **YAML** (YAML Ain't Markup Language): a human-readable format used for each slide deck's front matter (title, date, options, and so on).
* **Quarto**: the publishing system that renders the `.qmd` files into the final slides.
